title: All Ways to Climb With Steps of 1, 2 or 3

concept.title: List the ways instead of counting them
body: A staircase of `n` steps is climbed with moves of 1, 2 or 3 steps, and the **order of the moves matters**: `1+2` and `2+1` are different ways. Counting them is easy with a formula, but here every way must be **printed**, so we build them with backtracking: keep the moves so far in a list and the number of steps still to climb.

The loop tries the small steps first, so the ways come out in dictionary order of their text (`1+1+2` before `1+2+1`). This is the usual shape of "list all solutions": the recursion stops when nothing remains to be done, and the list `current` is restored after each try.

statement: A staircase has `n` steps. In one move you climb 1, 2 or 3 steps, and you must reach exactly the top. Print all ways to climb it, each as the moves joined with `+` (for example `1+2`), in dictionary order, one way per line.
outputFormat: All ways in dictionary order, one per line.
hints: Keep a list of the moves made and the number of steps that remain.
When nothing remains, record the list as a text.
Try the moves 1, 2, 3 in this order, but never a move larger than the steps that remain.

explanation: The recursion keeps the moves made so far. When the remaining height is 0 the list is recorded; otherwise the moves 1, 2, 3 that fit are tried in order, and each is removed again after the recursive call.
solution.complexity: Time O(number of ways * n), space O(n) besides the output.
